rows.en:
Heh, I'm glad.
That my turn came around so early...{p}

Tell me, {a}...
Does the newspaper club always stay this late?
...To be honest with you.
I don't really approve of staying at school until so late.
Because the school after hours is dangerous in all sorts of ways.
Once the dismissal time has passed, and all the students are gone...
...when the hour they call omagatoki, the hour of meeting demons, arrives.
This place stops being the school we know.
The number of steps on the stairs changes...
The sound of a bouncing ball comes from the empty gym...
Eerie stains rise up on the classroom walls...
After school, this place becomes a dreadful space ruled by evil.
Heh...
Is it still a little early for omagatoki?
But the hour of evil is already close at hand.
Dusk...
The threshold of night...
What I'm about to tell you is the story of a student who went through something terrifying in the school at night.{p}

...There was once a boy at this school named Yasuhiro Nanase.
I hear he was cheerful, and good at making people laugh.
Every class has at least one, doesn't it?
The kind of boy both the boys and the girls like...
But you see, Nanase had a bad habit that even the teachers couldn't do anything about.
He... forgot things. All the time.
Textbooks, notebooks, homework, gym clothes, his lunch......
They say not a single day went by without him forgetting something.{p}

Heh...
{a}?{p}What about you?
I forget things a lot
I don't forget things much
I never forget anything

I see...
So you can't say it never happens.
Then again, perhaps that's normal...
But you had better be careful.{p}

Heh...
It goes without saying that it's better not to forget things.{p}

Nanase must have thought so too.
Every time a teacher scolded him for forgetting something, every time everyone laughed at him, he must have sworn to himself that tomorrow, for sure, he wouldn't forget a thing.
And at last, that day came.
The day Nanase didn't forget anything...
It was in his third year, I believe.
His textbooks...
His homework...
His lunch...
He had every last thing.{p}

"How about that?
Now you all know I can do it when I try, right?"
Nanase looked thoroughly pleased with himself...
You'd think he had worked some great miracle.
Everyone was so astonished, and
"It's gonna rain spears tomorrow!"
...that was the joke going around.{p}

But you see, Nanase was forgetful after all.
It happened after school that same day...{p}

Nanase went home in high spirits, but the moment he opened his bag to do his homework, it hit him.
He had art homework due the next day, but he had left the bag with his art supplies at school.
Heh heh heh...
That kind of forgetting happens too, doesn't it?
Nanase panicked.
After all his bragging to everyone that day, he had gone and forgotten something after all.{p}

Tell me, {a}?
Have you ever forgotten something like that?{p}What would you do at a time like this?
Go to school to get what I forgot
Get to school early the next morning and do the homework there
Give up on the homework

You'd go back for it.
Heh, I thought you'd say that.

...Nanase was the same.
He sprang up from his chair without thinking and headed for the school.
Any other homework would have been one thing, but he wasn't confident he could finish art homework first thing in the morning.

Besides, he was bad at getting up early.
He always woke up just barely in time not to be late, which is why he always forgot something or other.{p}

Seen under the moonlight, the school looked completely different from the way it did in the daytime.
It should have been familiar, yet it was like a place he was visiting for the first time...
The hushed, silent building even began to seem like some huge creature holding its breath in the darkness.
Every time the lukewarm wind brushed his cheek, a chill ran down his spine, and in a corner of his mind he heard a voice, almost a warning, telling him to turn back.{p}

Even so, Nanase didn't try to turn back.
The one thing he wanted to avoid was everyone finding out he had forgotten something.
After bragging so much, they'd laugh at him all the more.
Besides...
A high schooler saying,
"I was too scared of the school at night to go get what I forgot"
...would be a little embarrassing, wouldn't it?{p}

Nanase slipped into the building so no one would see him, and walked down the dark hallway with nothing but the feeble glow of the emergency lights to guide him.
All he could hear were his own footsteps...
With every step he took, a chill crept up from the floor under his feet.
He had made it this far, driven only by the wish not to be humiliated, but...
As he listened to his dry footsteps echoing down the empty hallway, I imagine he grew more and more uneasy.
"Maybe I should've just gotten up early and come tomorrow..."
They say he muttered something like that.
Heh...
It's a little late to be saying that now, isn't it?
He hurried down the hallway, climbed the stairs...
And after all that, Nanase finally reached his own classroom.{p}

Then he timidly opened the door and stepped inside, peering in as he went.
With the moonlight coming in through the windows, and his eyes used to the dark, he could make out the room without turning on the lights.
At this rate, he'd be done sooner than he thought...
I imagine that's what went through his mind.
But you see, the moment he looked at his seat by the window, Nanase was stunned.
There was nothing hanging on the hook at the side of his desk.{p}

Tell me, {a}.
You know the annex next to the new school building, the one just for special classrooms like the art room and the music room?
Until that annex was added on, most of the classes that used special classrooms were held in the old school building.
They say that back then, every time students changed rooms, they had to walk along the walkway between the two buildings, which was nothing but a simple rain cover over a row of boards...
Yes...
The art room where Nanase's art supplies were was in the old school building too.
{a}...?{p}Have you ever been inside the old school building?
Yes
No

Oh, you've been inside?
You're a naughty one, aren't you...
That place is off-limits.
You'd be in serious trouble if a teacher caught you.{p}
...Let's get back to the story.{p}

Nanase headed for the art room.
"I'm fine, I'm fine.
I'm not scared one bit."
That's what he kept telling himself, of course.
Through the dark, lonely hallway, down the stairs...{p}
He came to a lone door at the end of the first-floor hallway.

Heh, the door that leads out to the walkway.
Nanase took one deep breath and slowly opened the door.{p}

Outside the door, pitch-black darkness stretched out before him.
All he could faintly make out was the narrow path of boards stretching away, and just a few of the posts that held up the rain cover.
Farther on, both the path and the posts melted into the dark, and the old school building was lost in it completely.
He couldn't see it at all.
It's like it leads down to the bottom of the abyss...
That's what Nanase thought.
As if one false step would have the ground swallow him up on the spot...
Even wild ideas like that came into his head.

Creak... creak...
Only the creaking of the boards sounded strangely loud.
Creak... creak-creak...
...That's weird.
Does one person walking really make this much noise...?

Skreek.
And...
On top of the footsteps, I think I hear something like metal grinding, too...
Without realizing it, Nanase had started walking softly, muffling his steps.

Creak, clatter...
The strange noises gradually grew louder.
He couldn't see anyone, but someone besides Nanase was walking along the walkway.

...Someone's coming.
From in front of me...?
Or from behind...?
Thunk, clatter-clack...

...In front!
It's coming this way from up ahead!
The instant he thought that...

The boards shook with a rattle.
Nanase stopped dead without meaning to.
Over toward the old school building, he could dimly see something like a human figure.
It seemed the figure was walking toward Nanase.

...A teacher making the rounds?
But nobody would make the rounds without even a flashlight...
Then who on earth could it be?
The figure looked unsteady, swaying feebly, and yet it gave off a strange sense of presence.

Creak...
The creaking of the walkway sounded like a scream.
...Maybe whatever's coming from over there isn't human.
Nanase couldn't shake that thought.
Heh heh heh...{p}What would you do at a time like this?
Ignore it and keep going
Wait and watch for a while
Run away as fast as I can

I see, you'd wait and watch.
Nanase did the same.
He stood stock-still on the spot, watching to see what would happen.
...Or rather, he was frozen stiff with fear.{p}

As Nanase watched, holding his breath, the figure came slowly toward him with a dull clanking and rumbling.
As if surfacing out of the darkness, its shape gradually became clear.
And when it came close enough that he could make out even the details of its face...

"..........☆"
Nanase caught his breath in spite of himself.{p}

What appeared from the far end of the walkway was a soldier in a tattered military uniform.
The soldier was pushing an empty cart, staring into space with exhausted, hollow eyes.
Then he stopped in front of the trembling Nanase, his hollow eyes flashed with a sudden glint, and he glared at him with a terrifying face.
"Wh-waaaaugh!"
Nanase ran for his life.

If he could just make it to the new school building, maybe he'd be safe...
I imagine he was thinking something like that.
But you see, the soldier kept coming after Nanase, wherever he went.
Even into the new school building itself...{p}

He tore down the first-floor hallway...
Before he knew it, the end of the hallway was drawing near.
Ahead of him was nothing but a single classroom door and the stairs up to the second floor.
Behind him, the soldier was still coming after him.
Run upstairs...
Or hide in the classroom...
Tell me, {a}.{p}What do you think Nanase did?
He ran up the stairs
He hid in the classroom
He stopped running and charged at the soldier
Without thinking, he had chosen a desk far from the door.

Clank... rumble...
From the hallway came the sound of the cart the soldier was pushing.
...Please, just go on past!
Nanase prayed with all his heart.
But then...

...Clunk.
The sound stopped dead, and the classroom door was flung open.{p}

Clack... clack...
The soldier's footsteps, drowned out until now by the noise of the cart, echoed through the hushed classroom.
And then...

Knock knock...
From across the room came the sound of a desk being lightly rapped.
And after that,
"Not here..."
came a muttering voice...

Next, a desk was rapped a little closer.
"Not here either..."
Knock knock...

"Not here either..."
The soldier was checking under the desks, coming closer and closer.
One at a time, slowly, surely...
And then...{p}
Knock knock.

At last came the sound of the desk right next to his being rapped.
"Not here either..."
...Oh no, this is it. What do I do?
Nanase shut his eyes and trembled.{p}
Clack... clack...

The soldier came closer and closer.
One step, two steps...
Clack.
The footsteps rang out right beside him.
...It's all over!
Nanase squeezed his eyes shut even tighter.

But then...
For some reason, there was no sound of the desk being rapped.
Even after he stayed still for a while, he couldn't hear a single sound.
...Maybe I'm safe.
Slowly steadying his breathing, Nanase opened his eyes.
And at that very moment!{p}

"Waaaaaaah☆"
Nanase's scream echoed through the school in the dead of night.{p}

Nanase wasn't found until the next morning.
You know the cherry tree behind the old school building, don't you?
I heard it was somewhere around there...
They say he was lying unconscious on top of the cart.{p}

...His hair had turned completely white.
When the teachers heard what had happened to Nanase, every one of them made a sour face.
And then someone muttered,
"Not again..."
...That's what they said.{p}

Heh heh, you see, the truth is...
That wasn't the first time the cart had been taken out of the storeroom.
Apparently it happened fairly often.
Usually, though, it was no more than the cart being pulled out, dragged all over the schoolyard, and then left abandoned in a corner of it...

Heh heh heh...
Haven't you ever heard a story like this...?{p}

They say that from the war years until just after the war ended, one part of this school was a first-aid station where the dead and wounded were brought in.
The gym overflowed with the wounded, and day after day an appalling number of people died.
The bodies were carried out right away and thrown into a pit dug in one corner of the schoolyard.
Carts loaded with corpses went back and forth without end.
...During the war, it seems they simply buried them as they were.
After the war ended, the number of bodies went down, they say...
Even so, the black smoke of burning corpses, thick with the stench of rot, never stopped rising.{p}

I...
I think the cart Nanase was put on was the one they used back then to carry the bodies.{p}

Heh heh...
It's still here at this school, you know.
Along with the grudges of all those dead... in the old school building.
Why would it be in a place like that, you ask...?
You'll understand if you come.
Well, {a}...{p}You want to see it, don't you?
Yes, I do
No, I don't

Heh heh...
I thought you'd answer that way.

Well then, shall we go take a look?
Hm?
A flashlight, you say...?
You do worry a lot, don't you, {a}?
It isn't that dark yet, so we won't need one.{p}

...Look, that's the old school building.
It's been left abandoned for ages since it stopped being used, hasn't it?
They say it's so run-down it could collapse at any moment.
Heh heh heh, do be careful not to get hurt, everyone...
Well then, shall we go inside?{p}

...Oh my, it's darker than I expected.
But it's all right.
We only have to go straight down this hallway...
...That's right.
The cart is there.
Why would something like that be in a hallway, you ask?
Heh heh... you'll understand when you see it.{p}

...There, we've arrived.
This is it.
See? It's obvious at a glance, isn't it?
This used to be part of the hallway, but now it's been turned into a storeroom.
And the cart in question is right here, too.
Look closely.
See this stain spreading around here...
Don't you think it looks rather like the color of blood?
There are marks here, as if something clawed at it.
I wonder who made these scratches?{p}

Murmuring that, Iwashita fell silent.
She seemed to be staring hard at the far end of the hallway that had become a storeroom.
What's the matter with her?
"Iwashita...?"
"……………………"
No answer.
...Maybe she didn't hear me.
Okay, one more time.
"Iwashita★"{p}

"…………Oh, I'm sorry.
I was miles away."
Even as she said it, Iwashita kept staring at that one spot.
What on earth could be there?{p}
"Yes, just a little something..."
Okay, I'll head back ahead of you
Come back with us, Iwashita
I'll wait for you, Iwashita
"Iwashita, come back with us too."

What is Iwashita thinking?
Staying behind alone in a place like this is dangerous...!
"Oh my, {a}, are you worried about me?
...Thank you.
But I'll be fine.
Don't worry about me..."{p}
...Huh? Iwashita★
Hey, wait.
Looking into the darkness at the end of the hallway where Iwashita had vanished, I let out a sigh.{p}

"Jeez, she's hopeless.
Hey, {a}...
Like she said, let's head back without her."
Urged on by those words, we left the old school building, leaving Iwashita behind.{p}

...Partly because it was cloudy, it was quite dim outside.
Without anyone saying a word, we all stopped and looked back at the old school building...
The old school building, finally slated for demolition.
It was an eerie place even in broad daylight, and now, at dusk like this, Iwashita was inside it all alone...{p}

I'm starting to get worried.
What if she's in some kind of danger...?
...Should I go back to the old school building?
Just as I thought that, someone tapped me on the shoulder.
Startled, I turned around, and there...{p}

"Oh dear, you're still hanging around here?"
"Iwashita...★"
What★
When did she come out of the old school building...?
"What's wrong?
Don't stare at me like that.
...Oh, I see.
You're startled because I suddenly appeared, aren't you?"
"…………Yes."
All I could do was nod.
After all, I'd been watching the old school building closely, and I never saw any sign of Iwashita.{p}

"Heh heh...
You're so trusting, {a}.
The old school building is this run-down.
There are any number of handier ways out."
"...Ways out?"
...Oh, so that's all it was.
She really gave me a fright.
"That's right, ways out.
Though whether they're paths the living use, I couldn't say...
Heh heh heh..."

"Iwashita...?"
"Oh my, you took me seriously again.
Heh heh, what a sweet child."
That meaningful smile...
Somehow, it sent a chill through me...

"I'm joking, just joking…………
It's more comforting to think so, isn't it?
...Come, let's go back.
I can't wait to hear the next story.
Heh heh heh...
It's already the witching hour.
But no one can escape now.
The second story has only just ended...
The seven wonders have barely begun, after all..."{p}

Oh my, just like Nanase.
Then you'd better listen carefully to my story.{p}

Oh my, that's wonderful.
You're the first person I've ever met who says they never forget anything.
You're amazing, {a}.
I can't help but look up to you.{p}

That's one way to do it, I suppose.
But you see, Nanase was different.
He sprang up from his chair and headed for the school.
...Naturally.
Think about it.
Any other homework, maybe, but do you really think you could finish art homework first thing in the morning?
Even someone good at drawing would find that a bit hard, wouldn't they?
A picture slapped together for lack of time would never be accepted as homework.{p}
Give up, you say...★{p}Do you really think that's all right?
Yes
No
...Well then, I'll ask you again.{p}If you left the things you need for your homework at school, what would you do?
Go to school to get what I forgot
Get to school early the next morning and do the homework there

...I see.
So you're just like Nanase.{p}

A lazybones...?
Little Miss Lazybonesina, then.
He gave up on his homework too.
Going back to school for his art supplies, getting up early the next morning to finish the picture at school... he found both such a bother he couldn't stand it.
It'd be easier to just let everyone laugh at him...
Maybe once he thought that, he felt relieved.{p}

Nanase crawled into his futon early and fell asleep.
...I wonder how long he'd slept.{p}

"Yasuhiro...
Get up, Yasuhiro, come on!"
It was Nanase's mother's voice.
...Ugh, so noisy...
Is it morning already...?
Thinking that, he looked at the window, and...?
Outside the window, it was pitch dark.
"What the heck, it's still night..."
"What are you talking about?
You've got a make-up class now, don't you?"
"A make-up class...?"
"The school just called.
They said it's a make-up class just for students who keep forgetting things, and you're the only one who hasn't shown up..."
...Was there a make-up class like that?
No, maybe there was...
Did somebody mention it?
And I just forgot...
"Come on, get up.
Hurry up and go."
"...Okay."{p}

Seen under the moonlight, the school looked completely different from the way it did in the daytime.
It should have been familiar, yet it was like a place he was visiting for the first time...
The hushed, silent building even began to seem like some huge creature holding its breath in the darkness.
Every time the lukewarm wind brushed his cheek, a chill ran down his spine, and in a corner of his mind he heard a voice, almost a warning, telling him to turn back.{p}

For a moment, Nanase thought about turning back.
But just then, he saw a light in a window of the old school building.
...That must be the classroom where they're holding the make-up class.
I can see lots of people in there...
Oh, so there are plenty of others in the same boat after all.
Once he thought that, Nanase suddenly perked right up...
Humming a tune, he went into the old school building.
...Say, {a}.{p}Have you ever been inside the old school building...?
Yes, I have
No, I haven't

Oh, you've been inside?
You're a naughty one, aren't you...
That place is off-limits.
You'd be in serious trouble if a teacher caught you.{p}

When Nanase reached the classroom...
The make-up class had already started.
When he secretly peeked in through the window, everyone was listening intently to the lesson.
Is it all right if I go in now...?
I feel like I'd just be interrupting...
Heh heh heh...
Walking into a classroom in the middle of a lesson does make your heart pound a little, doesn't it?{p}

Nanase was hovering in front of the classroom door.
And then...
"You there...
Don't just stand around out here, come inside."
With those words, someone tapped him on the shoulder.{p}

He turned around, and there stood a male teacher he recognized.
"Oh, yes, sir..."
Urged on by the teacher, Nanase reached out to open the door.
But you see...{p}

...What was this teacher's name?
Which class did he teach again...?
I'm sure it was…………
The teacher's hand resting on his shoulder was icy cold.
"What's the matter?"
The teacher asked, peering into Nanase's face.
He definitely recognized that face.{p}

...That's right, it's Mr. Miyata, the Japanese history teacher.
He taught me in first year...
But…………
"…………☆"
Nanase couldn't help staring hard at the teacher.
The teacher's face was unnaturally pale.
I'm sure Mr. Miyata…………!
Just then, a single trickle of blood ran down from the teacher's forehead.

Mr. Miyata, last year...☆
The one standing before Nanase's eyes was a teacher who was supposed to have died in an accident a year ago.{p}

...No way☆
Startled, he looked into the classroom, and the students seemed strange too.{p}

...You understand by now, don't you?
That's right.
What Nanase had wandered into was a ghost classroom.
A ghost classroom...
They say that there, the dead who cling too strongly to this world to pass on study the things they couldn't do while they were alive.{p}

"Waaaaaaah☆"
Nanase screamed before he could stop himself.
That was a mistake.
Hearing the scream, the ghosts in the classroom noticed Nanase.
...Oh no!
By the time he thought that, it was too late.{p}
All of them turned to look at Nanase at once.{p}
I have to run...☆{p}

Nanase shook off Mr. Miyata's ice-cold hand and fled as fast as he could.
The moment he broke into a run, the ghosts in the classroom came chasing after him.
"Wait!"
"You're one of us, aren't you?"
"Come along with us..."
Eerie voices, beckoning, trying to drag him in, clung to him from behind.
...Stop it!
...Stop it!
...Stop it!
Nanase covered his ears and ran for his life.
All but tumbling, he raced down the stairs and burst out of the old school building...{p}
